Prompt Injection.question: Does your system pass user-supplied text directly into the LLM prompt, or does it process content from untrusted external sources such as documents, emails, or web pages?
applies_if: User-supplied content is concatenated into the LLM prompt without structural separation from system instructions
The system ingests and processes documents, emails, or web content that reach the LLM context via the Context Assembler
The LLM can invoke tools or APIs, and instructions embedded in user input could influence which tools are called
No adversarial input filtering or prompt injection detection is applied at the Input Guardrail

Sensitive Information Disclosure.question: Does your RAG knowledge base contain confidential, personal, or sensitive information that not all users should be able to retrieve?
applies_if: The knowledge base contains PII, employee records, financial data, or confidential business documents
Different users have different access rights but the vector store applies no per-user document-level filtering
The LLM could reconstruct sensitive training data when prompted with specific extraction queries
Responses are returned to users without a content filter that screens for unintended data leakage at the Response Interface

Supply Chain.question: Does your system rely on third-party pre-trained models, open-source ML libraries, or externally sourced datasets for training, fine-tuning, or retrieval?
applies_if: The LLM is a third-party hosted model or an open-source model obtained from a public registry such as Hugging Face
Embedding models or ranking models used in the Retriever are sourced from external providers without integrity verification
ML framework dependencies (e.g. transformers, LangChain, llama-index) are updated via package managers without a pinned, audited bill of materials
Training or fine-tuning datasets include any content from third-party providers, public data repositories, or web scraping pipelines

Data and Model Poisoning.question: Is data ingested into your knowledge base sourced from web scraping, user uploads, or any partially untrusted automated pipeline?
applies_if: Knowledge base documents are ingested automatically from external websites, user submissions, or third-party APIs without a review gate
The vector store can be updated at runtime without human review or content moderation of incoming documents
Fine-tuning datasets include user-generated, crowd-sourced, or publicly scraped content
Retrieval results are not screened for adversarial or manipulated content before inclusion in the LLM context by the Context Assembler

Improper Output Handling.question: Are LLM-generated responses passed to downstream systems, rendered in a browser UI, or used to construct API calls or database queries without sanitisation?
applies_if: LLM output is rendered in a web interface and could contain injected HTML, JavaScript, or markdown that executes in the browser
Model responses are used to construct SQL queries, shell commands, or further API or tool calls
A downstream service consumes LLM output as structured data (JSON, XML) without schema validation
No output sanitisation or content filter is applied at the Response Interface before delivery to end users or downstream systems

Excessive Agency.question: Does the system grant the LLM the ability to call external APIs, modify databases, execute code, or take any action beyond read-only document retrieval?
applies_if: The Orchestrator can invoke tools, plugins, or functions based on LLM decisions with no mandatory human checkpoint
The LLM can create, update, or delete records in connected data systems or backend services
Tool permissions granted to the LLM exceed the minimum necessary for its defined task
An autonomous multi-step agent operates without a human confirmation step before consequential or irreversible actions

System Prompt Leakage.question: Does your system prompt contain confidential business logic, operational instructions, persona definitions, or proprietary information that must not be disclosed to users?
applies_if: The system prompt encodes business rules, safety restrictions, or capability limitations that must remain confidential
The system prompt references internal API endpoints, credentials, or environment-specific configuration details
Users interact directly with the LLM and could craft queries designed to elicit or reconstruct the system prompt contents
Persona instructions or safety filter details are embedded in the prompt rather than enforced at the application or guardrail layer

Vector and Embedding Weaknesses.question: Does your RAG pipeline use a vector database or embedding model, and are any documents or queries sourced from potentially adversarial or untrusted channels?
applies_if: The vector database is populated from external, user-contributed, or partially untrusted document sources without integrity checks
The embedding model has not been evaluated for adversarial robustness or susceptibility to nearest-neighbour manipulation
Retrieval results are not validated for relevance or screened for adversarially crafted content before passing to the Context Assembler
A single malicious document in the Data Store could systematically bias retrieval results across a wide range of user queries

Misinformation.question: Could users act on AI-generated responses without independent verification, or does the system operate in a domain where inaccurate outputs carry regulatory, financial, or safety risk?
applies_if: The system provides advice or information in regulated domains such as healthcare, legal services, financial advice, or HR decisions
Users are likely to treat LLM outputs as authoritative facts rather than probabilistic suggestions requiring verification
The knowledge base may contain outdated, conflicting, or domain-specific information the LLM could misrepresent or hallucinate
The system does not surface confidence scores, source citations, or hallucination warnings alongside responses at the Response Interface

Unbounded Consumption.question: Is your system accessible to external users or automated pipelines, and could a single actor trigger a high volume of LLM inference requests?
applies_if: The system is exposed via a public API or web interface without per-user or per-IP rate limiting
Automated processes, third-party integrations, or batch pipelines can submit requests at machine speed without throttling
No token budget, context-window cap, or per-session cost ceiling is enforced by the Orchestrator
A single large or adversarially crafted query could consume disproportionate compute, memory, or cost resources
